This writ petition is filed seeking for following relief :-
"Issue a writ of mandamus directing the 3rd respondent to send reference under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act by considering the petition filed by the petitioner as per Annexure-D and forward the amount of compensation awarded t o w a r d s a c q u i s i t i o n o f s c h e d u l e p r o p e r t y v i d e r e f e r e n c e No.KIADB/LAQ/2617/2023-24 the notification issued under Section 28(6) of the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board Act as per Annexure-C."

entities.text: Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Sri P.M. Siddamallappa, learned counsel submits that petitioner was owner of schedule property bearing Sy.no.122/P10 measuring 1 acre 15 guntas situated at Konaghatta Village, Kasaba Hobli,
Doddaballapura, Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, acquired by respondent for formation of industrial area.

It was submitted that petitioner was holder of agreement of sale dated 08.03.2018 executed by respondent no.4 after receiving sale consideration of Rs.46,00,000/- out of total amount of Rs.52,18,750/-.

It was submitted that as owner had not come forward to execute sale deed in favour of petitioner, NC: 2023:KHC:44989 he had filed O.S.No.131/2021 against respondent no.4 before Principal Senior Civil Judge, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, which was pending.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bangalore Rural District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In view of pendency of suit and dispute regarding title over property, petitioner had filed an application before respondent no.3 on 07.09.2023 for reference of dispute under Section 30 of Land Acquisition Act.
Since same was not considered, petitioner was constrained to approach this Court and sought for issuance of direction for consideration of his application.

3. Learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent no.1 and Sri. P.V. Chandrashekar,
learned counsel for respondent nos.2 and 3 would submit that filing of said application without stating whether award was passed or otherwise, would not be justified.
In any case, respondent no.3 would consider petitioner's application after passing of award, if not already passed within reasonable time.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner and perused writ petition papers.

5. From above submission it is seen that petitioner's grievance is about respondent taking note of petitioner's interest in land acquired, at time of passing award and for reference of dispute for adjudication.
Admittedly petitioner has filed application seeking reference.
Even if award is not yet passed, same would not come in way of respondent considering application as and when award is passed.

6. In view of above, writ petition is disposed of directing respondent no.3 to consider petitioner's application at Annexure-D, in case award is not already passed immediately after passing award and if award is already passed, within two months from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

Sd/-
